chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwān narrated from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the glance of the Angel of Death (peace be upon him). He said: 'Do you not see a group of people sitting together, then sudden speechlessness afflicts them, so none of them speaks? That is the moment in which the Angel of Death glances at them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the sign of the Angel of Death's glance according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the 'glance of the Angel of Death' is defined not as a physical event but as a sudden spiritual paralysis where a group falls silent, signaling the onset of death. This highlights the Shia understanding of death as an immediate, divine intervention that severs worldly connection, serving as a potent reminder for *zuhd* (asceticism) and constant mindfulness of the Hereafter.
